description: Browses the most-subscribed, trending subreddits right now, with no keyword. Returns a `subreddits` list (each with name, title, subscriber count, description, type, and NSFW flag) plus an `after` cursor for paging. `include_details=true` fills `created` on up to the first 10 subreddits; otherwise `meta.unavailable_fields` names any field the page left null.

after.description: Opaque pagination cursor: the previous response's `after` value, exactly as it was returned. The format is not stable, and a hand-written Reddit fullname loses the paging depth the cursor carries. Absent on the opening page. A null `after` on a response means there is no next page; it does not by itself mean the listing is complete, because Reddit often stops serving a busy listing long before it runs out. That final response carries `listing_status`: `complete`, `truncated` or `unknown`, and only `complete` means nothing is missing.

include_details.description: true fills created on up to the first 10 items, from one extra read per item, so the page answers slower. false or omitted (default) returns the list page as served, where those fields may be null and `meta.unavailable_fields` names them.

limit.description: Maximum items returned, 1 to 100. The API clamps out-of-range values; the endpoint default applies when omitted.

name: reddit_subreddits_popular
title: List Popular Subreddits
